evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Besides pricing, do you have any questions or concerns specifically you would like answered on this call?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep followed up on packing-services concern: 'Do we have any special consideration items?' and followed with 'How do your furniture?' and probed on volume: 'how much stuff do they have? Is everything full?' Also explored timing concern multiple times: 'So, I know they've been there for a bit do you feel like three and a half hours for packing is a lot'
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: I do want to do packing services [customer stated]; rep confirmed and built into discussion
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floor/stories (second floor origin, third floor destination with elevator), rooms (one bedroom, 725 sq ft), walking distance (straight stair), special considerations (sofa, loveseat, two twin beds, patio furniture), additional stops (none), closure kitchen/pantry/coat closet packed

top_strength: Rep systematically gathered all necessary logistics details and genuinely probed the customer's two main concerns—packing feasibility and the tight move deadline—by asking follow-up questions rather than brushing past them.
coaching_note: Rep never delivered the quid-pro-quo time-box framing or waited for a yes, and never summarized/reflected back the customer's concerns before pivoting to logistics—both Section 2 and Section 1 gaps that should be addressed in every call.
